text:
acme_ops: Seeing sudden 502s from the hosted inference endpoint in us-east-1. Starts ~08:12 UTC, lasts ~10-15s, repeats every 5-7m. No changes from our side. Logs show TLS handshake timeout for a bunch of requests. Any ideas?

julie_support: thanks — can you share one example request id and an approximate time? tagging SRE.

acme_ops: request id 01H7Z9A2-8 at 2026-03-16T08:12:14Z. stack: POST /v1/generate -> 502, error in gateway: handshake timeout.

julie_support: quick look at our edge traces shows a cluster of TLS handshake timeouts at the same time. Also seeing a spike in resolver failures (truncation / SERVFAIL) from our edge. @ingrid_sre can you pick this up?

ingrid_sre: starting a resolver trace. Can you run both these from your side and paste outputs?

```
# UDP
dig +time=2 +tries=1 endpoint.redwood-hosted.com @8.8.8.8

# force TCP
dig +tcp +time=2 endpoint.redwood-hosted.com @8.8.8.8
```

acme_ops: pasted outputs — UDP returns an answer but with `;; Truncated, retrying in TCP`, TCP queries intermittently time out (connection timed out). Example: `;; communication error to 8.8.8.8#53: end of file` then no A record returned under TCP.

deploy-bot: Route53 healthcheck (us-east-1-resolver) detected SERVFAIL / TCP timeouts between 2026-03-16T08:12:10Z and 08:12:18Z — alert generated.

ingrid_sre: hypothesis: after the cert rotation we triggered a batch of parallel model metadata fetches and cache-misses which produced a burst of DNS queries from a narrow set of egress IPs. Upstream resolver started truncating (EDNS0) and then rate-limited TCP fallbacks, causing our edge to fail TLS handshakes because name resolution for the backend stalled. This looks like resolver-side rate-limiting / truncation + simultaneous cert/connection churn, not a TLS cert chain mismatch.

alex_ops: mitigation plan I just applied: 1) short-term in-process answer cache for the hot model prefixes (30s TTL) 2) route the affected customer IP range to our alt-resolver pool (different egress fabric) 3) backoff the cert-prefetch concurrency that caused the spike. Also raised resolver TCP connect timeout on the gateway from 1s -> 3s while we stabilize.

julie_support: applied the routing patch and cache — acme_ops can you confirm if you still see 502s? :eyes: :thumbsup:

acme_ops: no 502s since the change — traffic looks stable for ~30m. Thanks for the fast turnaround!

ingrid_sre: follow-ups: we'll open a short postmortem. immediate action items: 1) add metrics for resolver truncation+tcp-fallback count and correlate with handshake timeouts, 2) smooth cert rotation probes so we don't create large simultaneous DNS churn, 3) increase concurrency capacity on alt-resolvers and add per-egress smoothing, 4) add a customer-facing blurb about transient 502s during rotations.

julie_support: recording this in the incident tracker and notifying the oncall handoff. thanks everyone.

# diagnostic snippets collected by SRE:

```
# tcpdump (edge egress) sample:
15:12:14.123456 IP edge-egress.20345 > 8.8.8.8.53: UDP, length 512
15:12:14.124000 IP edge-egress.20345 > 8.8.8.8.53: Flags [S], seq 0, win 65535, options [mss 1460], length 0  # TCP fallback attempt
# curl showing TLS handshake timeout to backend when resolution stalls:
curl -v --connect-timeout 5 https://backend-infer.redwood/ -H 'Host: endpoint.redwood-hosted.com'
* Rebuilt URL to: https://backend-infer.redwood/
*   Trying 10.20.30.40...
* TCP_NODELAY set
* connect to 10.20.30.40 port 443 timed out
* Closing connection 0
* TLS handshake timeout (likely because DNS didn't return address)
```
